source_paper_text:
Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop
Collected by Julien Codsi

Problem 31. Geodesic separator for planar graphs (From Julien Codsi)

Is it true that every planar graph has a balanced separator (where no remaining component
has more than half the number of vertices) that is the union of two shortest paths? It is known
that 3 are enough [48]. Actually, the proof in [48] gives something stronger. There exists a
tree decomposition where every bag is the union of 3 geodesics and where the intersection of
every bag is the union of 2 geodesics. Therefore, if we relax the definition of balanced to “no
component has more then 2/3 of the vertices” then the answer is yes.

Problem 33. Restricted induced Ramsey for the triangle (From Daniel Carter)

Is there a {K_6, odd hole}-free graph G such that all 2-edge-colorings of G contain a
monochromatic triangle? (If so, what about {K_4, odd hole}-free?)
target: Prove or disprove: every finite simple unweighted planar graph G has a vertex separator S=V(P1) union V(P2), where P1 and P2 are each shortest paths between their own endpoints in the original graph G and may intersect, such that every connected component of G-S has at most |V(G)|/2 vertices.
title: Half-balanced planar separator formed by two geodesics
